selected.rationale: Adding delay to the webapp→Ordering.API call propagates unbounded latency into the order-submission user flow. This can exceed client timeout or cause double-submit if no timeout/retry guard exists.

Basket reads/writes hit Redis synchronously; a delay stalls every cart operation and can escalate basket API failures if no Redis timeout or fallback is configured. It directly affects checkout availability.
Losing the checkout integration event from Basket.API to RabbitMQ silently breaks order initiation after the basket is cleared. This exposes missing persistence/retry for event bus publication.

HTTP loss on the critical basket edge makes carts unavailable and may trigger non-idempotent retries or dropped cart actions. It exposes missing retry/recovery behavior on a revenue-impacting dependency.
Mobile order submission is blocked when requests to Ordering.API are lost; without BFF retry/idempotency the user cannot place orders. This is an availability loss on the purchase path.
Catalog APIs are on the main browsing path; latency here propagates directly to page render and mobile browsing. A missing client timeout would make the storefront hang when catalog is slow.
Delayed identity API calls slow login and authentication-related operations and can cascade into repeated auth timeouts. This exposes missing timeout handling at the auth boundary.
Loss on catalog integration events leaves downstream services with stale product/price data. It reveals missing outbox/retry behavior for publishing domain updates.
